grade_reason: Barr has spoken about AI several times since 2025, always as a race with China to be won through energy (especially coal) and data centers, or as a jobs concern; none of these acknowledges catastrophic risk, so the level is D. No statement dismissing catastrophic risk was found, so not F.
corrections: Not strictly a correction, but the existing file says no AI statement in his own words was found. There are some (all level D, listed above). The existing file's statement that no press release title concerns AI still holds: the 14 January 2026 item 'Barr in HFAC: Kentucky Coal can Boost U.S. in AI Race' is in his Video Gallery, not Press Releases, and the 5 June 2026 press release mentions AI only in its body (the earlier run read titles only).
notes: 10 web searches ran (7 that had not run before plus 3 follow-ups); none refused. The search on the 23 September 2026 senators' letter was not run, because the addendum says its signer list is already verified and Barr (a House member) is not on it. No statement on superintelligence, extinction, AI safety, pause, slowdown, China AI talks or self-improving AI was found. Left out: (1) Debate with Charles Booker hosted by WKYT, reportedly 19 October 2026: a search result quoted Barr as saying "I understand the concerns, and Americans shouldn't ever have artificial intelligence threaten their job", and a Lexington Herald-Leader piece reportedly quotes him calling himself a "free market guy" on AI job losses. I could not open the source (newsfromthestates.com returned 403 / Cloudflare), so the wording and date are unverified; it would be level D (jobs) anyway. (4) barr.house.gov/ai-plan is titled 'AI Plan' but the page body is 'Andy Barr's Plan to END The War on Coal, Restore Kentucky Energy Dominance' with no AI text visible. Context, not his action: the pro-AI super PAC Leading the Future spent at least $750,000 supporting Barr (Axios, 22 May 2026, search result only).
